- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and news volume remains high, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 30-day horizon.
- Model underestimates when sentiment shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment changes) — adjust up by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of historical mean, model is biased high; apply downward correction of 3–5%.
- Sentiment change >0.67 in 3 consecutive days triggers a “mean reversion” signal — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is flat (±0.33) for 5+ days, model tends to drift — apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overconfidence.
